newsitem.title: UK: Stg under pressure as politics regain upper hand.
newsitem.headline: Stg under pressure as politics regain upper hand.

text.p: The pound weakened sharply on Wednesday as U.S. traders took fright after an opinion poll showed a slump in the opposition Labour party's lead just over a week before election day, traders said.
An ICM poll in the Guardian newspaper showed Labour's lead fell from 14 to five points, the first time the opposition's lead has fallen to single digits since November 1993.
A rolling Gallup poll in the Daily Telegraph gave a conflicting picture, putting Labour 21 points ahead, an inrease of five in a week.

European foreign exchange traders were unfazed, and the pound firmed in morning trading, but it suffered from a wave of selling when U.S. markets opened. It shed three pfennigs and over a cent and a half on the day.
A victory for the opposition Labour party has been discounted but analysts reckon British markets will be susceptible to selling if the May 1 election results in a hung parliament.

"The pound seemed to take it in its stride until the U.S. opened," said a senior trader at a German bank here. "We saw some heavy cable (sterling/dollar) sales go through, which triggered general pressure on sterling."
At 1609 GMT the pound traded at $1.6230, down from $1.6370 in late European trading on Friday. Against the mark it was at 2.7768/78 against 2.8050/60. Sterling/yen eased to 204.50 from 206.40.
Dealers said stop loss sell orders were triggered at $1.6280, accelerating the pound's decline.
"The U.S. seems to have taken a much more grim view on the opinion poll in the Guardian than the European market, which is in wait-and see-mode until next week," the trader said.
Sterling/yen selling also weighed on the pound. Buying of sterling for yen on the back of the pound's relatively more attractive yield has been one of the engines behind the pound's rally.
